name: Stonega
summary: Little Stone Mountain watchtowers near Big Stone Gap from the 1910s; the later CCC iron tower was torn down in the 1970s and its parts reportedly lie on private land.
design: Iron tower with an iron cab, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps; the earlier tower was wooden
status_note: Torn down in the 1970s; a 2019 local history places its parts on private cabin land.
agency: Virginia Forestry Department, later Jefferson National Forest

access.note: The parts reportedly lie on private cabin property atop Morris's Butt, per a 2019 local history. Ask the owner before going near.

events.note: Start of the 1910 to 1917 window for the first watchtower on Little Stone Mountain. The exact date is not known, and the site is only the author's best guess.
By 1917 the tower had been moved to the ridge top of Little Stone Mountain, where a second tower was built with the state forestry department.
Iron tower built by the Civilian Conservation Corps on National Forest land. The author gives no exact date and believes it went up not long after 1933.
Torn down in the 1970s. The account gives no exact year; 1970 marks only the start of that decade.
